recipes.name: Tofu Cheesecake
ingredients_raw: 2 (12 ounce) packages extra firm tofu, drained and cubed

steps.text: Preheat an oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
In a blender or food processor, combine tofu, sugar, vanilla, salt, vegetable oil, and lemon juice. Blend until smooth. Pour into the pie crust.
Bake in the preheated oven until slightly brown, 20 to 30 minutes. Remove from the oven to cool. Refrigerate until chilled.

raw_recipe.headline: Tofu Cheesecake
raw_recipe.description: Tofu is blended until smooth to create this vegan alternative to cheesecake.

review.reviewBody: I've tried this. The trick is to Add REAL vanilla flavoring to the tofu the day before, the sugar, and lemon juice. Blend this together with food processor or super high powered blender. If your blender sucks you wont get a good consistency. Once blended, pop this in the fridge and let it set over night or the next 2 days so the Vanilla flavor can overpower the bean taste. If you like a little kick to your cheesecake, add some other flavoring (rum, coconut, strawberry, almond etc.) and let the tofu marinate in the chosen flavoring over night. Add the other ingredients after the marinating and then bake. Tastes JUST like cheesecake!

I enjoyed this recipe very much, but it may not be for everyone. The texture is creamy and soft like a cheesecake, but the distinct taste of tofu is subtly in the flavor. I also did a few modifications.

I added 2 eggs and baked for 35 minutes because even 30 was not enough. I am still slightly debating with myself if I should've done 40 for a more firm texture.

You do not need to use silken tofu, but you have to make sure the tofu is blended. My blender is kinda weak, so I manually mashed the tofu with a fork and mixed in all ingrediants minus eggs (saved half of vanilla extract for later). I did that until the consistency was like cottage cheese. Then, I blended the eggs in the blender, and slowly added more crumbled tofu. When the load was a bit too much for my blender, I scooped up some soft tofu from the bottom and pushed more solid tofu down. This forced the solid tofu to get blended. Once it was all silky smooth, I scrapped everything out of the blender with a spatula back into the mixing bowl and added the rest of the vanilla extract, then let it set in fridge overnight. Mother said it smelled of vanilla that following morning.

The baking part went surprisingly well. I poked the cake with a toothpick to check if done after 25 minutes and it was too liquidy. 10 more minutes made it well. I used a cake pan and the sides came off surprisingly easy!

Definately gonna bake again and maybe add a few more modifications.

I made this using 1 silk tofu & 1 extra firm tofu. I also used butter for oil. I added 1 egg & 1 cup coconut for a friend who loves coconut ;, too. For crust I used 1 c.crushed pretzels; 1/4 c.sugar; 1/4 c. butter & 1 c. coconut. I placed the crust in a bundt pan pressed against the outer side & bottom. I poured the batter in and cooked from 30 min to an hour until well set. After cooling I released w/knife the crust from the pan and the set "custard" from the inner side. After turning the pan over a base plate I placed it in the frig to cool. I cut 25 pieces. Really, really good ;)
Used extra firm silken tofu for a creamier texture and baked a little longer than suggested so that it would form up more. It’s a new, easy favorite!

This is my first time trying this recipe. I was using a hand mixer at first but quickly realized that I needed something better. I popped it in my Ninja blender and it came out nice and creamy. 
 I added cocoa and a little mint as I blended too. I am allergic to gluten so I started with a homemade, gluten free graham crust, then spread chocolate chips on the crust and poured in the tofu mix. I had some dried cranberries that I sprinkled on top before trying (Christmas time). Delicious together. You could really add just about any topping. Nice gluten free/dairy free alternative.

Worked great, albeit with my modifications. I used 700g of smooth soft tofu, replaced the oil with almond/hazelnut butter, and halved the sugar with sucralose. Combined it with my immersion blender and would have made a tasty pudding as-is. Not identical to a dairy cheesecake in flavour or texture, but it's sweet, tangy, and creamy. It fills that same niche without the prohibitive cost of cashews or cream cheese. Very pleased. I can't imagine extra firm tofu is the best choice but I haven't tried it.

the husband and i are total dessert heads. in an effort to stave off the extra pounds, i try to only make vegan desserts with whole ingredients and without a lot of added sugar. i thought i would try this one to go with some fresh blueberry sauce i had leftover from breakfast, and it definitely exceeded our expectations. the first time i made it, i halved the sugar and doubled the lemon juice, then baked for 50 minutes, and it came out great. i will trade the density of real cheesecake for the healthfulness of organic non-gmo tofu and lack of guilt any day!!! i'm making this pie again with lime juice and lime zest instead of lemon to try and emulate the feel of a key lime pie. thanks for a good, SIMPLE vegan recipe.

We prefer to make Tofu Cheesecake with 5 ingredients in a blender: 1/2 brick tofu, 1/2 package cream cheese (can use low fat), 1/2 cup sugar, 2 eggs, 2 teaspoons vanilla. Pour into a prepared graham cracker crust. Bake at 375 for 45 minutes. Cool to room temp. Top with berries (canned or fresh) & - optional: whipped cream. Yum. Store in the refrigerator. This recipe was a demo at the grocer's for a tofu company. It's a great light lo cal cheesecake that pretty much appeals to all. Not vegan, however. Easy to remember: measure 1/2 of 3 ingredients and 2 of the other 2 ingredients + berries.

This is a great recipe for starters, but mine was runny and did not really taste like "cheesecake." Remade it with following changes: added two large eggs and two tablespoons white flour, plus the grated rind of a lemon, and mixed in food processor. THOSE results were very NY Cheese-cake-ish, and a great pareve desert with strawberries.

I was really impressed with how well this turned out, I really liked it and it was gone by the next day. I think draining the tofu is a really important step. I wrapped the block of tofu in paper towels and then wrapped that in cloth towels before placing a cutting board on top with weights on top of that. I read it's advised to drain for 30 min or so but I did it for several hours, changing out the towels when they got soaked. By the end, the block of tofu felt like a dense block of cheese. I am definitely going to make this again and again. Also, there was only firm and extra firm at the store and neither of them were Silken but the extra firm, after proper draining came out so smooth and creamy!

I think it's a great base. What I mean by that is that while it's almost complete on its own, I feel like you can definitely add more to it to alter the flavor to your liking. (about to make this again tonight and planning to zest a lemon into the batter!)
I highly recommend using Speculoos Cookies instead of Graham Crackers for the crust. I just use the whole package of Trader Joe's Speculoos Cookies and 8 tablespoons of Earth Balance. That's it. Simplicity is key.

I only used one package of silken tofu, pressed and drained of excess water, and a little nondairy creamcheese. I used a vanilla bean and some orange zest. I forgot the oil but it was probably in the creamcheese anyway. I also used one egg. It was more than could fit in my crust, so the extra was placed in a little soup crock and eaten without a crust.
Fail horrible recipe it did not bake

It came out sort of okay, was a little too dry. It didn't really taste too much like "cheesecake", but more like just a sweet sugary dessert. It looks good though. I didn't really taste the soy, so that was good. I ate it without any fruit on top, so maybe will try some to see if it helps with the dry texture while eating it.
Very tasty, although you can swap the 1 cup sugar with 1 cup of dates

This recipe is excellent! However the type of tofu that is needed to excute this properly is not listed other than "extra firm". You'll need silken extra firm tofu to achieve the "cheesecake" like texture. I substituted the sugar for whipped honey(2 1/2 tbsp) and used a vegan pudding powder mix that was cheesecake flavored (2 tbsp available in Whole Foods)

I added 1/4 cup of flour. After an hour it was still very soft so I left it for another hour at 250. The texture isn't consistent and it kinda separated a bit. It's a bit wet. Flavour is somewhat like cheesecake. I made a strawberry sauce for on top.
Quick and easy, good basic recipe for cheesecake, I flavored with lime juice and added shredded coconut for a key lime flavor

This isn't a perfect recipe, but it IS a very good base on which to experiment.

I used silken firm tofu (all I could find). I also accidentally left out the oil, and I'm glad I did. And after reading some of the reviews, I cut the sugar down to 3/4 C. 

The texture was great. Not like a dense cheesecake, but it *is* like some lighter cheesecakes I have had. I didn't love the flavor by itself, but we topped with a dollop of cherry pie filling and it was FANTASTIC! Especially because I used a chocolate graham crust. 

This was a hit. Next time, I'm going to play with irish cream type flavoring, or perhaps go strongly on vanilla and almond extract.
Love it! It’s not cheesecake but it’s very good. I added strawberry topping and fresh strawberries. I had to bake almost 50 minutes.
